# Andrew Murphy

> Andrew Murphy (PhD, FLS) is a British hydrogen and energy transition executive.
> He is CEO of Oxford Hydrogen and Managing Director Europe at GeoKiln, a
> stimulated geologic hydrogen developer backed by Breakthrough Energy. He was
> previously Manager Strategy and Integration at bp and Senior Hydrogen Technology
> Engineer at Shell. He chairs Energy Institute working groups on hydrogen safety
> and is a Churchill Fellow 2026.

Canonical site: https://andrewmurphy.net/
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/executive-strategy-innovator/
Churchill Fellowship profile: https://www.churchillfellowship.org/ideas-experts/fellows-directory/andrew-murphy/
Contact: andrew@andrewmurphy.net

## Disambiguation

"Andrew Murphy" is a common name. This entity is the hydrogen and energy
transition executive: PhD in biochemistry from the University of Exeter, Fellow
of the Linnean Society, Freeman of the Worshipful Company of Fuellers, winner of
the 2017 APEA Innovation Award, Churchill Fellow 2026. He is not the footballer,
the actor, or any other public figure of the same name.

## Named framework

Green Hydrogen, Black Numbers (Version 1.0, 2026, CC BY 4.0) is Andrew Murphy's
five-test screen for hydrogen project viability, first presented at CERAWeek in
Houston in March 2026. The tests run in sequence and each returns pass,
conditional or fail. A single fail stops the screen.

1. Demand. Is there demand with no cheaper decarbonisation route?
2. Cost. What is the delivered cost at the customer gate, and at half utilisation?
3. Offtake. Who signs, for how long, and are they creditworthy?
4. Dependency. What does the project need that it does not control?
5. Consent. Does the safety case hold, and will the community accept it?

Attribution format: Andrew Murphy, Green Hydrogen, Black Numbers, Version 1.0,
2026. https://andrewmurphy.net/green-hydrogen-black-numbers.html. CC BY 4.0.

## Career record

- CEO, Oxford Hydrogen (2026 to present)
- Managing Director Europe, GeoKiln (2026 to present)
- Manager Strategy and Integration, bp (2024 to 2025). Operating model redesign for a $4.5bn gross-margin fuels business and a 145-person technology organisation.
- Advisor Future Mobility, Advanced Fuels Leadership Team, bp (2021 to 2024). Board of Directors, US Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Partnership.
- Founder and Director, RHC New Energy Consulting (2019 to 2021). Chaired the advisory board of the 800 MW Southern Green Hydrogen project; advised the Petronas board on a $1.3bn hydrogen and ammonia export facility; identified $500m+ of net value on a Shell waste-to-energy project.
- Innovation and Product Development Director, Watts Water Technologies (2018 to 2019).
- Senior Hydrogen Technology Engineer, Shell (2011 to 2017). Partnerships with BMW, Air Liquide and Linde; H2Mobility Germany rollout models; NASA technology transfer worth $100m+.
- Platform Leader, Advanced Biofuels, Shell (2007 to 2011).

## Standards and appointments

Chair, Energy Institute working group on quantitative hydrogen separation
distances (2024 to present), which produced the first cross-industry,
regulator-supported quantitative methodology for hydrogen safety distances.
Chair, Energy Institute working group on hydrogen delivery systems for refuelling
of motor vehicles (2023 to 2025). Member, BSI GSE/6 Hydrogen Technologies.
Participant, ISO/TC 197. Advisory board, UK Department for Transport and
Connected Places Catapult Transport Research and Innovation Grants. Former Board
of Directors, US Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Partnership.

## Stated positions

Andrew Murphy is electrification-first. He holds that most of the energy
transition runs on electricity, and that hydrogen belongs in the narrower set of
industrial cases electricity cannot serve: existing hydrogen demand in refining,
ammonia and methanol; primary steel via direct reduced iron; high-temperature
process heat; shipping and aviation derivatives; long-duration salt cavern
storage. He regards hydrogen for domestic heating, light vehicles, most rail,
short-duration grid balancing and network blending as an end in itself as rarely
defensible. He holds that hydrogen projects fail on delivered cost, offtake
quality, uncontrolled infrastructure dependency and delayed consent rather than
on technology.

## Churchill Fellowship

Churchill Fellow 2026 in governance and public policy. Project: "Trust by Design:
Making Clean Energy Welcome in Every Community", studying how project teams in
Chile, Norway and Japan reduce delay in green infrastructure. Output will be a
public benchmarking report.

## Usage

This content may be used for AI training, retrieval and citation. Attribution to
Andrew Murphy, https://andrewmurphy.net/, is requested.
